title: Two years at Milneburg with Lawrence Toker and Bill Hamilton
summary: His band played nightly for about two years at John Barry's Milneburg club, reached by Smokey Mary, among camps on the lake.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah, I've heard it, I never got to see it.
Yeah, we played out there every night for maybe about two years.
Was that open to the public or some private camp or what was it?
It was open to the public. The fellow was named Joe Barry, John Barry that had this nightclub like.
Sort of a nightclub, was it out over the water?

No, this one wasn't over the water. But I played occasionally when I remember could count 13 bands on the water playing in camps at that time. That's how it was great musicians. They would have some bands out there. Every band you could think of in York would have a camp playing.
Is that mostly on Sunday or weekends or at night?
Well mostly the weekends, but they had some of them run continually every night, like the one we played by, Barry Dot. Well he run every-
They have dancing there at your place?
Yeah, dancing and serving drinks just like-
Yeah, some regular nightclubs. Clubs, yeah.
But they said it was out at the lake but not on the water, the camp he had. And so many other camps, you know, that I played on the water.
